chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you. I had a fat ram to slaughter as a sacrifice. So when I took it and laid it down, it looked at me, so I pitied it and was moved with compassion for it. Then I slaughtered it.' He said to me, 'I would not like you to do so. Do not raise something (for slaughter) and then slaughter it.'

key_terms.رَحِمْتُهُ: I pitied it / felt compassion for it
key_terms.رَقَقْتُ عَلَيْهِ: I was moved with tenderness/softness of heart towards it

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette regarding raising an animal for sacrifice in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) advises against raising an animal specifically for slaughter, noting that the animal's direct gaze can evoke pity and cause emotional distress to the owner. This teaching emphasizes mercy and avoiding unnecessary emotional burden during the act of sacrifice. The Imam's preference highlights the spiritual value of *rahmah* (compassion) in Islamic rituals, encouraging believers to cultivate a gentle disposition even in acts of worship.
